Executive summary

Main finding
Thesis AI acquired users quickly, but conversion and recent acquisition momentum are weak.

The dataset shows 671 users by August 2026. Monthly signups rose from 2 in February to a peak of 267 in May, then fell to 95 in June, 84 in July and 56 in August. That is a roughly 79% decline from the May peak to August.

Monetization is still very limited: 8 paid users represent about 1.2% of the user base. The subscription-status chart shows only 2 active users, indicating either a narrower definition of active subscription or a data consistency issue that should be investigated.

Priority actions

  • Identify what drove the May acquisition spike and test whether it can be repeated.
  • Build a free-to-paid conversion funnel and measure where users drop off.
  • Reconcile the paid-plan field with subscription status before using either as a revenue KPI.
  • Segment onboarding by field of study and emphasize APA 7 workflows.
  • Standardize category labels before the next dashboard refresh.

Charts

New users by month

Monthly acquisition rose sharply to a May peak, then declined for three consecutive months.

Cumulative user growth

The user base reached 671 by August 2026, but the slope has flattened since May.

Free vs paid users

Only 8 of 671 users are marked paid, implying a paid share of about 1.2%.

Top fields of study

Computer Science and Economics lead the displayed fields, but inconsistent capitalization splits some categories.

Citation style share

APA 7 dominates citation style usage at 74.7%, followed by Harvard at 12.8%.

AI autonomy

Human-in-the-loop usage dominates at about 91.8%; autonomous usage is about 8.2%.

Subscription status

Only 2 users are marked active while 669 are inactive, which does not align cleanly with the 8 paid users.

Data-quality observations

  • Case inconsistencies: "Computer Science" and "computer science" appear separately; "Law" and "law" also appear separately.
  • Possible spelling issues: "Havard" should likely be "Harvard" and "IEE" may need validation against "IEEE".
  • Status inconsistency: 8 users are paid, but only 2 are active. These may be different concepts, but the business definitions should be documented.
  • Field-of-study counts are fragmented: cleaning capitalization and aliases could change the top-10 ranking materially.

Recommended next analysis

  1. Create a monthly funnel: sign-up -> activated -> retained -> paid -> renewed.
  2. Measure cohort retention by signup month to see whether the May cohort remained engaged.
  3. Compare paid conversion by field of study, citation style, and autonomy preference.
  4. Analyze billing-cycle-end dates to identify upcoming renewals, expired subscriptions, and churn risk.
  5. Add product-usage metrics such as projects created, documents uploaded, citations generated, and sessions per user.
Scope note: This report is based on the seven charts supplied in the conversation. Underlying row-level source data was not supplied, so calculations and interpretations use the values visible in those charts.
